newsitem.title: MOROCCO: EU won't rule out new fishing accord with Morocco.
newsitem.headline: EU won't rule out new fishing accord with Morocco.

text.p: Visiting European Union Fisheries Commissioner Emma Bonimo said on Monday Brussels does not rule out reaching a new fishing accord with Rabat in future despite Morocco's reserves, the official MAP news agency said.

Rabat had repeatly said the current accord which is to expire in 1999 will not be renewed, arguing that Morocco's fish catches fell by 30 percent in recent years due to what it described as "EU fleet irrational exploitation" of its fish resources.

"Morocco is a sovereign state...But it is not excluded that a new accord will be reached after 1999 because Rabat should take into account its political, economic and commercial ties with Europe," MAP quoted Emma Bonino as saying.
Bonino, who made a brief statement, was attending the opening ceremony of a two-day fish industry exhibition in Morocco's financial centre of Casablanca.
After months of wrangling, Morocco and EU signed a four-year fish accord in February 1996, under which Brussels pays the equivalent of $162.5 million a year in fees for fishing rights.
Morocco also obtained that the period to allow stocks to recover be extended to four from initial two months.
Both parties also agreed that starting from the second year of the accord the number of European vessels allowed in the Moroccan waters would be cut to 552 units from the current 590, officials said.
